sourceNote: Every count here is transcribed from a cited row of that table. Nothing is inferred from a sibling model: two cards with four fiber connectors are 32 and 40 respectively because the line rate differs, so a connector count tells you nothing. A device the table could not settle carries unknown:true and no number - a wrong ceiling silently caps a wall, so unknowns stay unknown.

labels.note: # is the port number within the nearest named device; {name} is that device's name. A port's label comes from the nearest named device upstream of it - CVT, then card, then processor. With nothing named upstream there is no processor-derived label at all, and the per-screen portLabelTemplatePrimary / portLabelTemplateReturn keep labelling exactly as they always did.

devices.name: MX40 Pro
devices.note: 40 via the 4x 10G optical outs. In 20-port mode OPT 3/4 are copies of OPT 1/2; in 40-port mode they carry ports 21-40. The summary spec sheet leads with 20, which is why two research passes both came back 20.

devices.name: MX30
devices.note: 2x 10G OPT at 10.3125 Gbps: OPT 1 transmits Ethernet ports 1-10 and OPT 2 is its copy channel, so both carry the unit's own copper and a box on either adds no ports.

devices.name: MX20
devices.note: 2x 10G OPT: OPT 1 transmits Ethernet ports 1-6 and OPT 2 is its copy channel - the unit's own six ports again, never more.

devices.name: KU20
devices.note: 1x 10G OPT output is documented, but no sheet states what it carries - no port mapping, no copy statement - so no box hangs off it until that is settled.

devices.name: CX40 Pro
devices.note: 5GBASE-T. Its one optical port is 40Gbps - a rate the CVT8-5G takes - but no sheet states what the OPT carries, so no box hangs off it until that is settled. Same shape as the KU20.

devices.name: CX80 Pro
devices.note: 5GBASE-T. 2x 40Gbps optical ports carrying the unit's own copper - OPT 1 corresponds to Ethernet 1-8 and OPT 2 to 9-16, each equal to 8x 5Gbps ports. 40G trunks take the CVT8-5G and only the CVT8-5G.

devices.name: VX400
devices.note: Confirmed against the hardware; one dealer page claiming 6 is wrong. Max 2.6 million px; its sheet states no per-port figure. Two fiber outputs copy / back up the four Ethernet ports, but the sheet states NO optical rate, so under the 10G rule no box hangs off it.

devices.name: VX400 Pro
devices.note: Max 2.6 million px, 650,000 px per port on 8-bit. 2x 10G OPT carrying the unit's own four ports: in Output mode OPT 1 sends them and OPT 2 copies or backs them up; in the input modes the OPTs are video in / loop out instead. The port count is 4 in every mode, and a box adds none.

devices.name: VX600
devices.note: Max 3.9 million px; its sheet states no per-port figure. OPT 1 is a documented 10G output copying the six Ethernet ports, so one box can take the same six out on fiber. OPT 2 also copies/backs them up but its sheet names no rate for it, so it is not counted as a trunk.

devices.name: VX600 Pro
devices.note: Max 3.9 million px, 650,000 px per port on 8-bit. 2x 10G OPT carrying the unit's own six ports (Output mode: OPT 1 sends, OPT 2 copies or backs up; input modes repurpose them). The port count is 6 in every mode.

devices.name: VX1000
devices.note: Max 6.5 million px; its sheet states no per-port figure. OPT 1 is a documented 10G output copying the ten Ethernet ports. OPT 2 also copies/backs them up but its sheet names no rate for it, so it is not counted as a trunk.

devices.name: VX1000 Pro
devices.note: Max 6.5 million px, 650,000 px per port on 8-bit. 2x 10G OPT carrying the unit's own ten ports (Output mode: OPT 1 sends, OPT 2 copies or backs up; input modes repurpose them). The port count is 10 in every mode.

devices.name: VX2000 Pro
devices.note: 4x 10G OPT carrying the unit's own twenty copper ports: OPT 1/2 send Ethernet 1-10 / 11-20 and OPT 3/4 copy or back them up, so no box adds a port. OPT 1/2 are self-adaptive and become video INPUTS in the input+output working modes, leaving only OPT 3/4 as outputs; the port count is 20 in every mode.

devices.name: MCTRL4K
devices.note: 16x Neutrik Gigabit Ethernet on the unit. 4x 10G OPT carry them again - OPT1 transmits Ethernet 1-8, OPT2 transmits 9-16, OPT3/4 are their duplicate channels - so a box on any OPT is another place to plug into the same sixteen.

devices.name: MCTRL660 Pro
devices.note: 2x 10G OPT: OPT1 corresponds to all 6 Gigabit Ethernet ports and OPT2 is its backup, each optical port equal to 6 Gigabit ports - the unit's own six again. In fiber converter mode the OPTs become inputs; the port count is 6 either way.

devices.name: MCTRL660
devices.note: Copper only: 4x RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet, 650,000 px per port. Its HDMI OUT / DVI OUT are video cascade connectors, not fiber - no box hangs off it.

devices.name: MCTRL R5
devices.note: 8x RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet, 650,000 px per port on 8-bit and 325,000 on 10-bit; loads up to 3840x1080@60Hz. Supports port and screen rotation (10-bit input does not rotate). 2x 10G OPT carry the same eight ports - OPT 1 copies Ethernet 1-8 and OPT 2 is the copy channel of OPT 1 - so a box adds nothing.

devices.name: MCTRL700
devices.note: 6x RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet, 650,000 px per port; loads up to 1920x1200@60Hz. No optical ports at all, so nothing hangs off it.

devices.name: MCTRL600
devices.note: 4x RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet, 650,000 px per port; input up to 1920x1200@60Hz. No optical ports. Its sheet states no device total - 4 x 650k is arithmetic, so none is claimed.

devices.name: MCTRL300
devices.note: 2x RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet, 650,000 px per port; input up to 1920x1200@60Hz. No optical ports, no stated device total.

devices.name: MSD300
devices.note: Sending card that installs in a PC rather than a boxed controller; cascades over UART like the MCTRL300. Its own sheet: 2x RJ45 Gigabit Ethernet, 650,000 px per port, input up to 1920x1200@60Hz. No optical ports, no stated device total. The MSD300-1 is a different product with its own sheet and is not this entry.

devices.name: NovaPro UHD
devices.note: 16x Neutrik Gigabit Ethernet out, max 10,400,000 px. The four 10G OPTs add no ports - OPT 1/2 carry Ethernet 1-8 / 9-16 and OPT 3/4 are their copy/hot backup channels - so a box on any OPT is another place to plug into ports the back of the unit already has. Its spec publishes no per-port pixel figure; the Jr's numbers are the Jr's.

devices.name: NovaPro UHD Jr
devices.note: 16x Neutrik Gigabit Ethernet out, max 10,400,000 px - per port 650,000 px on an 8-bit source, 320,000 on 10/12-bit. Same OPT shape as the NovaPro UHD: OPT 1/2 transmit Ethernet 1-8 / 9-16 and OPT 3/4 are their copy/hot backup, available when all four OPTs are used for output. The OPTs add no ports.

devices.name: NovaPro HD
devices.note: 4x Gigabit Ethernet LED outputs; max 3840 px wide, 1920 px high - its sheets publish no total or per-port pixel figure, so none is claimed. It also has 4 optical fiber outputs no document maps to any port; they are 1G per Matt and useless with the CVT line, which is why no box hangs off this device.

devices.name: H2
devices.note: Documented as max OUTPUT CARDS, not physical slots - no NovaStar document states a slot count for any chassis.

devices.name: H9 Enhanced
devices.note: 10 for fiber/video cards, 5 for RJ45 sending cards - the sole card-type-dependent limit in the H series, so the chassis offers ten places and the limit drops to five as soon as an RJ45 card is in one. The 'two slots' explanation for it is unconfirmed.

devices.name: H20
devices.note: 20U. No Enhanced variant exists.

devices.name: H_20xRJ45
devices.note: Occupies 2 chassis slots, but the documented chassis limits are card counts and are NOT halved for it - an H15 still takes 10. Copper only: no OPT, so no CVT can hang off it at all.

devices.name: H_16xRJ45+2xfiber
devices.note: The OPT ports copy Ethernet 1-8 / 9-16, so they add no ports - a breakout box on OPT 1 is another place to plug into ports 1-8, not eight more ports. Both deliveries are real and both get used: patch the copper on the card, or take the same ports out at a box across the room. Counted as an RJ45 sending card against the H9 Enhanced limit; no document says which side of that split a mixed card falls on.

devices.name: H_4xfiber
devices.note: 4x 10G OPT at 8B/10B, one OPT = 8 Ethernet ports. Max 20,800,000 px. Cannot share a screen with RJ45 cards. Needs NovaLCT 5.4.8.

devices.name: H_4xfiber (enhanced)
devices.note: EIGHT 10G connectors but still four primaries - OPT 5-8 back up OPT 1-4 - and one OPT = 10 Ethernet ports. 4 x 10 = 40. Counting connectors gets this wrong in both directions: not 8, not 80. Max 26,000,000 px. Needs NovaLCT 5.8.0 or above.

devices.name: MX_4x10G fiber
devices.note: 64B/66B, 10 ports per fiber.

devices.name: MX_1x40G / CX_1x40G fiber
devices.note: The 40G card gives 8, not 40 - the fiber-to-logical ratio follows the line rate, never the connector. Its 40G trunk takes the CVT8-5G and only the CVT8-5G.

devices.name: CVT4K-S
devices.note: 16x Neutrik etherCON out on 2 OPT in. Its four LC connectors are TWO optical ports - LC is duplex - and counting them as four would double the box. Two OPTs at 8 per trunk is exactly its 16, so behind an H_4xfiber it delivers the lot; one box also takes both OPTs of an H_16xRJ45+2xfiber and delivers all 16 there, where CVT10s need two boxes.

devices.name: CVT10
devices.note: 10 ports on a 10.3125 Gbps 64B/66B trunk, 8 on an 8B/10B one - the box fans out whatever the trunk carries, so its real count is capped by the card's ports per fiber.

devices.name: CVT10 Pro
devices.note: Same figures as the CVT10: 1 OPT in, 10 ports on a 10.3125 Gbps 64B/66B trunk and only the first 8 from a 10G 8B/10B source.

devices.name: CVT8-5G
devices.note: 8x 5GBASE-T out on 1x 40G in. The 5G rate is what a port carries, not how many there are. The box for 40G fiber, and only for 40G fiber - it does not hang off a 10G OPT, and the 10G boxes do not hang off a 40G one.

devices.name: Tessera SX40
devices.note: 8 physical 10G connectors = 4 logical trunks, each auto-switching between the copper and fibre of a pair. It has NO 1G fixture ports of its own; fixtures hang off 10-port boxes, 10 per trunk - the XD by default (ruling, 2026-08-25: 'The sx40 by default has to use 10 port breakout boxes'), and the 12-port XD-S/XD-T still deliver only their first 10 here. Redundancy is opt-in per pair and pairs whole boxes, fixed adjacent - A backs up to B, C backs up to D - automatically; that is the only way redundancy runs on this device. It halves what is USABLE to 20 (10 per primary box), never the socket numbering: boxes A and C stay ports 1-10 and 21-30, and B (11-20) and D (31-40) carry their returns, because a tech patching socket 21 must find socket 21 on the drawing.

devices.name: Tessera S8
devices.note: Redundancy pairs fixed adjacent ports - 1 backed by 2, 3 by 4, and so on - automatically; that is the only way this device pairs. The rule arrived by name (2026-08-23): the SX40 does A to B and C to D, 'and S8 does 1to2 and so on'. It names the S8 only: the S4 and M2 still halve and still claim no pairing shape.

devices.name: Tessera T1
devices.note: Single output, so it cannot do closed-loop redundancy at all.

devices.name: Tessera SQ200

ports.unknownReason: Only "2x 100G QSFP28" is published, and the device is absent from Brompton's own capacity tool. No port count was found, and one must not be inferred from another Tessera.

devices.note: Redundancy pairs the same fixed way as the SX40 - adjacent outputs, A backs up to B, C backs up to D, automatically - while the output count itself stays unpublished. The pairing rule does not letter outputs nobody has counted.

devices.name: Tessera XD
devices.note: 10G in, 10x 1G out.

devices.name: Tessera XD-S
devices.note: 12 on the box, but both datasheets say only the first 10 work behind an SX40 - which is what the trunk cap produces. The XD-S product page contradicts them and claims 12 unqualified.

devices.name: Tessera XD-T
devices.note: Same as the XD-S: 12 on the box, first 10 only behind an SX40.

devices.name: Tessera QD-S
devices.note: 100G in, 12x 10G out. Those twelve are 10G trunks, not 1G fixture ports.

devices.name: HELIOS Standard 8K / 8K Extreme
devices.note: 8x 10Gb fiber SFP+, each feeding an RS12 that fans out to 12 copper ports. The 100G QSFP is an INPUT; there is no 100G output anywhere in the line. The 8 is trunks, where the SX40's 40 is fixture ports - the source table counts the two vendors at different tiers and does not reconcile them.

ports.conflictReason: The 2025/2026 documents say 2 and the 2023 spec sheet says 3. The source table records the conflict and does not adjudicate it, so neither number is the default - pick the one matching the document you are working from.

devices.name: HELIOS Jr
devices.note: 8x 1G copper SFP straight to tiles, with no switch layer at all. Not the same thing as "HELIOS (1G)", which is a switch port RATE behind a HELIOS Standard.

devices.name: RS12 / MSM4214X
devices.note: 12x 1/2.5Gb etherCON out; fiber ports 13/14 come IN from the HELIOS. Port 13 feeds outputs 1-6 and port 14 feeds 7-12; they are not interchangeable. 1G vs 2.5G is a per-port rate set by the tile, not a different port count. Its spare SFP slot cannot add a port.

devices.name: GSM4210P (legacy)
devices.note: The only device in the table where a spare SFP slot ADDS a real port. The MSM4214X explicitly cannot.
